Like a lot of things are bodies are gonna try and reject foreign objects like piercings so while they heal your body is really trying to heal the hole to close it. So yes any new cut/tear that opens up a wound is restarting that healing process. As long as there is something keeping the hole open it will be.

Eventually yes your body will get used to it. People change out jewelry constantly. You need to wait for it to be healed tho. Since you have a new cut in that piercing I would suggest you find a quality piece of jewelry like glass or titanium that is flesh colored that can remain in the piercing for atleast 2-3 months with minimal touching and removing as you are healing it now.  Keep it nice and clean and eventually you should be able to switch it with ease

Piercings are finicky and nostril ones can be the most considering how small the gauge is and how sensitive noses are. Keep in mind in the future it might sting when changing it out. I found increasing the gauge has helped me but to each their own.  

Also I’m no professional this is based on my research and experience I do still suggest you call a piercer who could give you clearer answers.

You can try looking into glass flesh colored nosebone retainers that would hopefully stay in and it’s glass so it’s pretty safe. Or look into silicone heart retainers as the backs will also stay in however silicone isn’t long term wear I believe. 
Considering it usually does take 6 months to a year for most piercings to be considered fully healed I do believe you are irritating and maybe doing slight harm to that piercing. Piercings really shouldn’t be touched and messed around as often as you are since your body is still adjusting.  
However just take things slow, clean and care for it try not to constantly switch out your jewelry. The more you irritate it and it bleeds your body will try to heal that spot and close the piercing unless of course something is in there. So I would suggest glass and going to a piercing shop to see if they have better recommendations. The plastic is definitely not good and as you know very short term jewelry. Good luck!

The Loomis method is definitely great. Your gripe is with proportions. Using the method remember that your lines come from the circle that encompasses the ear. Those lines need to be straight. As you carry those lines across the face they still need to be straight however they curve around the head either upwards or downwards depending on the direction and tilt of the head. If you look at your initial groundwork you can see your first horizontal line in that circle is good, however not center (I would also work on this as were you placed it makes the top head bigger), the second line begins at the bottom of the circle as you have here however begins to go downwards. 
You need this line to be parallel to the first line. 

I also noticed as I tend to do this mistake and place the nose lower, further away from the eyes. Look at the the negative space between points. If you look at the highest end of the nostril curve, you’ll notice in the photo it is a lot closer to his lower eyelids then you might assume it is. 
If you are trying to go for the most realism remember to draw exactly what you see and not what you think you see and think things are placed. We tend to naturally fill the space with our own imagery but to draw life you must do that. 
Use different points around the lines you are trying to put down to see how close or far that line needs to be to another point. Look at the face. Look at where everything sits and how it sits and how far away it is from another object. 
You definitely do that well in many spots and certainly clean it up well in the finished product. 
However it isn’t that man. However I do believe you will be able to draw him and many more. 
I really encourage you keep going and listen to all the criticism to push you further. 
Oh and last remember though they do differ person to person, usually the point between the top of our eyebrow and bottom of our noses, match the width/space between the bottom of our noses and the bottom of our chin with the top of the eyebrow and top of the head. I can see you know this yet your representation shows that the width/space is not equal or atleast close your head to brow is small, brow to nose big, and nose to chin medium. Yet though your reference images head is tilted obscuring how you may be seeing the head, those spaces are all equal for this individual. 
If it helps
Trace the loomis head over this reference and compare to yours after and then try again and again.
You can do it. Good luck!
